title: 2026-09-29-payments-procurement-kms-dpa-sla-preflight
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-09-29 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Recording ID: ff-20260929-7b3c
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Patel (Redwood SE), Rajiv Singh (ClearPath - Procurement), Leah Morales (ClearPath - Sec/Comp), Tom Baker (ClearPath - Finance), Alyssa Wu (ClearPath - Platform)

Summary:
Quick procurement + security preflight before legal receives redlines. Focus: MSA/DPA redline path, KMS/integration expectations, SLA tiers and pricing scenarios for pilot vs committed usage, and a short tech ask: run latency bench on our sample call flow.

Topics Covered:
- MSA redline governance and preferred exceptions
- DPA data residency and encryption (KMS/HSM)
- SLA tiers (uptime, p99 latency) and crediting model
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs and cost
- Benchmark request: 5k token churn, KV cache hit patterns
- Next steps and ownership for legal intake

Action items listed in call later in transcript. Transcript quality: medium (some auto-translation errors).

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for blocking time. Quick check, can people hear me?
[00:05] Rajiv (ClearPath): Yep, loud and clear. Thanks Maya, appreciate it.
[00:12] Jordan (Redwood SE): Hi all, Jordan here. I'll handle the technical bits. We kept this to 45-ish minutes, happy to go long if needed.
[00:20] Leah (ClearPath): Good. Our legal asked for a preflight so they don't get a surprise with redlines. Tom and I will flag finance and compliance items.
[00:28] Maya: Perfect. I'll share the MSA/DPA draft after this call, but wanted to run a few alignment questions so the redlines are targeted.

[00:32] Rajiv: First, parity question — is your platform offering hosted API sufficient for our PCI-scope workloads, or do we need Dedicated or Private? Our preference is to avoid on-prem unless necessary.
[00:40] Jordan: Short answer: for PCI-scope, we typically see customers choose Redwood Private (VPC) or Dedicated with strict network controls. Hosted can work if you require tokenization and strict DPA plus egress controls, but many enterprise payments teams opt for Dedicated to keep data pathing under their control.

[01:10] Alyssa (ClearPath): Can you clarify what you mean by Dedicated? Is that a managed cluster we can lock to our account?
[01:15] Jordan: Yes, Dedicated is reserved GPU pools - they're isolated and you can configure VPC peering, private endpoints, and we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) in that mode. Slight transcription note — sometimes the automation writes "Dedicate" but it's Dedicated.

[01:40] Leah: On KMS, our security team requires a list of key wrapping options and whether you support external HSMs or bring-your-own-key. We also need to know if Redwood logs any plaintext or if the key manages everything end-to-end.
[01:52] Maya: Good callout. We'll include the KMS whitepaper and an architecture diagram. Short answer: we support cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and optional HSM-backed keys via partner HSM integrations for Private. We also have a zero-logging policy for customer payloads in Dedicated/Private modes — we surface audit logs but not payload contents.

[02:20] Tom (Finance): On pricing, we need examples: pilot (month-to-month), then committed tiers for 6/12 months. Also, what's the billing model — token-based, or seat + throughput?
[02:30] Maya: Hosted is usage per token mostly, embeddings per unit, etc. Dedicated is a reserved capacity fee + usage overage for burst. For pilot we can do monthly without commitment; for committed capacity we can show blended pricing. We'll include at least three sample scenarios with expected cost per 1000 interactions.

[03:05] Rajiv: Legal side — we're likely to push for a few MSA exceptions: indemnity carve-outs, data deletion timelines, subprocessor list, and stronger SLA crediting. How flexible are you on indemnity?
[03:15] Maya: We try to be pragmatic. Typical path: smaller customers accept standard indemnities; for enterprise we can negotiate limited carve-outs and caps. We'll flag the exceptions we expect and ask legal to prioritize which ones are blockers vs negotiating points.

[03:45] Leah: On the DPA, we need the data residency clause: ClearPath requires EU data at rest and in transit for EU-customer data. Does Redwood support region-specific pinning?
[03:55] Jordan: Yes — we support region pinning on hosted where possible, and Dedicated/Private gives you full control to host in the EU region. Note: sometimes the auto transcript writes GD4N instead of g4dn when we mention instance families.

[04:25] Alyssa: Technical ask — our flow has a 5k token prompt plus a 1k token system context and repeated calls with KV cache hits ~40%. Can you run a latency benchmark on your H100 and g4dn-equivalent stacks using a similar pattern? We'll give you a sample dataset.
[04:38] Jordan: Absolutely. What would help is a sample of 100 representative calls and the sequence length distribution and peak QPS. We can stand up a test on Redwood Dedicated and compare hosted net latency. The benchmark will include cold-token and warm-cache numbers.

[05:10] Rajiv: And can we get p99 numbers? We need to compare to our internal SLOs.
[05:15] Jordan: We'll capture p50/p95/p99 and 99.9 if you need it. For Dedicated you can expect lower variance and better tail latency.

[05:45] Leah: On auditing — SOC 2, ISO 27001, penetration test cadence, and whether you provide raw access logs to customers for their auditors.
[05:56] Maya: We will share SOCtwo report excerpt, ISO summary, and pen test cadence. We provide audit logs including request-level metadata; payload is redacted unless you have Private with agreed logging. We'll include a sample log schema.

[06:30] Tom: Finance follows up — if we commit to a minimum monthly reserved capacity, what's the early termination look like and refunding?
[06:38] Maya: Typical contracts have pro-rated refunds for unused committed capacity only in limited circumstances; we'll include the typical termination tables. We can show a few commitment tiers with termination terms.

[07:02] Rajiv: Who's typically responsible for KMS billing? Do you charge for KMS usage or is that handled by the customer cloud account?
[07:09] Jordan: If you're using your cloud KMS, that's billed to your cloud account. If we manage keys in our environment for hosted customers, there's no direct KMS line item but it's part of the managed service fee. We'll make that explicit in the doc.

[07:40] Alyssa: Network egress — need to verify egress patterns and potential costs. We cannot assume low egress cost.
[07:46] Maya: We'll include egress patterns per deployment mode and sample egress engineering doc.

[08:05] Leah: Subprocessors — we want the full list + notification policy for changes.
[08:12] Maya: We'll attach a current subprocessor list and commit to 30 days notice for material changes; if your procurement needs longer notice we can discuss.

[08:40] Rajiv: For SLA credits, we typically require a monetary credit formula aligned to monthly fees. We also want p99 latency credits for API timeouts above threshold. Is that in your standard SLA?
[08:52] Jordan: Our SLA is usually uptime based with credits tied to monthly service fees. Latency SLOs are available as an addendum for Dedicated/Private, with p99 latency SLOs and crediting. We'll draft an SLA that ties credits to missed p99 thresholds where applicable.

[09:25] Tom: On tax and invoices, we need to know if Redwood bills from US entity or EMEA for EU customers for VAT reasons.
[09:33] Maya: We will include billing entity options and typical invoicing flow; final assignment depends on procurement geography and contracted entity.

[09:55] Rajiv: Timeline — legal wants to get MSA redlines within two weeks of receiving draft, and we aim to be under contract in 6 weeks if tests look good. Is that feasible?
[10:04] Maya: Feasible. I'll send the draft today, ask you to return prioritized redlines by 2026-10-13, and Jordan will run the benchmark by 2026-10-06. If everything meets expectations, we can align on a pilot start date the week of 2026-10-20.

[10:40] Alyssa: A couple of technical clarifications — do you persist KV cache between calls, and is that stored encrypted?
[10:47] Jordan: KV cache is typically in-memory per serving instance; cache persistence across requests is implemented at the platform layer for certain workloads, and when persisted it's encrypted at rest using the same KMS keys. We'll capture that nuance.

[11:12] Rajiv: Any competitors we should be comparing you to? We want a short list to show procurement.
[11:18] Maya: Sure — common comps: BigCloud AI managed endpoints, an open-source self-hosted runtime stack (customers sometimes build internally), and other inference platform vendors. We'll provide a short competitive matrix.

[11:40] Leah: Data retention — what is the default retention and can we specify retention periods per dataset?
[11:47] Jordan: Default retention is 30 days for logs, with options to shorten to 0 days for payloads in Dedicated/Private. For hosted, we offer configurable retention windows and a policy for deletion on request; we'll include the retention matrix.

[12:20] Maya: Okay, quick recap of owners for next steps. I'll list them and then we'll confirm on the call.

[12:28] Maya: Action item 1: Maya to share MSA/DPA draft and KMS whitepaper today.
[12:34] Rajiv: That would be great.

[12:40] Maya: Action item 2: Jordan to run latency/throughput benchmark using Alyssa's sample dataset and produce p50/p95/p99 numbers by 2026-10-06.

[12:50] Alyssa: We'll upload sample traffic to the secure share.

[12:56] Maya: Action item 3: Leah to send any mandatory compliance questionnaire items and prioritized redlines by 2026-10-13.

[13:05] Tom: Action item 4: Maya to provide three pricing scenarios: pilot, 6-month commit, 12-month commit by 2026-10-02.

[13:14] Rajiv: Can you also include an example SLA addendum for p99 latency credits?

[13:18] Jordan: Yes we'll attach an SLA addendum template.

[13:30] Maya: Anything else?
[13:33] Leah: One more — on vendor insurance: we need your current CGL and cyber insurance limits.
[13:39] Maya: We'll include certificate and limits.

[14:00] Rajiv: Thanks everyone, that's helpful. We'll expect the docs and then we'll get legal/finance back. If the benchmarks look good we'll aim for pilot sign-off.

[14:18] Maya: Great. I'll follow up with a calendar invite for the 10/6 benchmark review and 10/13 redlines checkpoint.

[14:30] Meeting ends.

Notes: Transcript has some automated mis-terms (e.g., "GD4N" for g4dn GPU family, "SOCtwo" for SOC 2). Cross-check attachments: [link] MSA_DPA_draft_v1.pdf, [link] KMS_whitepaper.pdf, [link] SOC2_excerpt.pdf, [link] sample-bench-requests.csv.
